02 / Local-first AI / Desktop software

NYRCNot Your Regular Companion

A desktop companion with persistent identity, memory, reminders, and optional intelligence. The provider can change. The companion stays.

1.0.0-rc.1 · Release candidate

  • Tauri
  • Rust
  • Svelte
  • TypeScript
GitHub ↗ — NYRCProject site ↗ — NYRC

The problem

A useful personal companion should retain its identity and everyday tools independently of a cloud account or a particular AI provider.

Who it is for

People who want a persistent desktop presence and practical local tools; developers exploring a shared interface for future companion devices.

Engineering challenge

Keep intelligence separate from authority. Typed actions and host confirmations bound what an AI suggestion or connected body can do.

Architecture

  1. Host: personality + memory + scheduler + tasks
  2. Optional intelligence → typed action proposals
  3. Host permission policy → supported actions
  4. Semantic Body API → desktop / virtual bodies

Simplified architecture based on repository documentation.

Technology choices

  • Tauri
  • Rust
  • Svelte
  • TypeScript

The stack above is documented in the repository. The architecture separates interface, execution or business logic, and persistence.

Documented implementation

  • Session timers and durable reminders with restart recovery
  • Pocket storage, saved aliases, routines, and personality settings
  • Provider-independent optional AI
  • Desktop and virtual bodies; authenticated loopback transport

Current limits

Unsigned release candidate. Native core acceptance is documented for macOS Apple silicon; other platforms require external desktop acceptance. Physical hardware adapters and voice recognition/synthesis are planned, not shipped.

Design takeaway

Separating identity, intelligence, permissions, and presentation allows the companion to remain useful with AI switched off.

This is an architectural interpretation of the documented implementation, not a measured outcome or a personal claim.
